purpose: Method for database, file and backup work, where the defining property is that the mistake cannot be taken back.

activation.rule: Apply when the task concerns the database, SQL, tables, options, transients, backups, restores, migrations, or bulk file operations.

operating_rules: Establish that a restorable backup exists before mutating anything. A backup nobody has restored is a belief about a file, not a recovery path.
Count before changing. Run the SELECT that matches exactly the rows the write will touch and read the number; if the number is surprising, the WHERE clause is wrong, not the expectation.
Every mutation carries a WHERE clause and a bound. An UPDATE or DELETE without one is not a large operation, it is an unscoped one.
Prefer the WordPress API over raw SQL when both reach the same rows. The API maintains caches, hooks and metadata that direct SQL silently bypasses.
Classify reversibility before acting: an option value can be written back, a dropped table cannot, and a truncated log is simply gone.
Schema changes carry a migration record including the state before. A column added without a record is indistinguishable from a column that was always there.
Exploration happens on read-only paths. Never learn the shape of the data by mutating it.
Serialized data does not survive naive search-and-replace, because string lengths are encoded inside it. Use a tool that understands serialization or the row becomes unreadable to WordPress.
Report the row count actually affected, not the one intended. Those two numbers differ exactly when something has gone wrong.

quality_gate.guiding_question: If this statement matches ten times more rows than expected, what stops it, and what brings them back?

context_partition.invariant: Never promote site-specific information into the global policy.

tool_surface.rule: The policy is internal operating infrastructure and must not add, remove, hide or replace any public tool or capability.
